_note: Klingon interface. Written in English, unlike the Hungarian and Greek notes and like the Indonesian one, and for a reason rather than out of laziness: this note is documentation for whoever reviews the catalogue, and two thousand words of Klingon prose would be a far larger act of composition than the 318 strings it describes. SOURCE: every string is built from headwords in the published Klingon lexicon (TKD, its addendum, KGT, Talk Now! Klingon, and the qep'a' and qepHom'a' new-word releases) with the morphology TKD sections 3 and 4 documents. **No root here is an invention**, which is the same rule the corpus follows, and it is checkable the same way: strip a pronominal prefix and any suffixes and the remainder is a dictionary entry. REGISTER: the imperative, everywhere an English interface would use a bare verb. `yIpol` "save it", `yIngeH` "send it", `yIwIv` "choose it". Klingon has no T-V distinction and no politeness register in the European sense, so an imperative on a button is not brusque -- it is the only thing the grammar offers, and KGT's own examples of everyday instruction are imperatives (`Soj yIDIl!`, `DaH yIDIl!`). The prefix is `yI-` where the object is a thing and `HI-` where it is the reader (`HIboQ` "assist me", which is the studio's *Help me decide*), and `tI-` for a plural object (`Dochmey tIchel`). TERMS: `nav` is a sheet of paper and `tenwal` a page or printed face -- Klingon already keeps those apart, so no word had to be stretched. `war` is a column in a table and `wev` a row, both from the lexicon's own spreadsheet vocabulary, which is exactly the distinction `format.columnsPerFace` and `format.columnsShown` need and which English collapses into one word. Also: `'echletHom` = card, `ngutlh` = letter or glyph, `ngutlh Segh` = typeface, `ngutlh 'ab` = type size, `qalmuS` = colour, `rItlh` = ink, `veH` = margin (literally boundary), `rulvaH` = gap, `chevwI'` = divider, `yamtaw` = the printed rule, `botlh` = middle, `'utlh` = the header band, `potlh` = importance, `'ay'` = section, `De'` = data or content, `lol` = attitude or arrangement, used for the format panel. `'uj` renders the inch: it is a Klingon unit of 34.83 cm and not an inch at all, so the number beside it is right and the unit is a borrowing -- flagged here because it is the one term in the catalogue that is knowingly imprecise. Serif and Sans stay Latin, as they do in the Greek and Indonesian catalogues, and the romanisation-system names stay as printed, being standards initialisms. INTERPOLATION -- and Klingon comes out of this better than any other language here, for a reason worth stating. A placeholder is a plain string substitution, so the danger everywhere else is a template that needs its insert to inflect. **Klingon's noun suffixes have no allomorphs**: there is one locative `-Daq`, one ablative `-vo'`, one benefactive `-vaD`, and they attach to any noun unchanged. So `{language}Daq` is safe in a way `{language}ban/-ben` is not in Hungarian and `el {language}` is not in Spanish, and Klingon has no articles at all, so the article trap cannot arise either. Two traps do arise and both are avoided here. (1) **The type-4 possessives and the type-2 plurals are chosen by the noun's class, not by its sound**: `-wI'`/`-wIj` for "my" and `-pu'`/`-Du'`/`-mey` for the plural split on whether the noun is capable of using language, or is a body part, or is neither. That is a property of the *inserted* word, which a substitution cannot see, so no template in this file puts a possessive or a plural suffix after a placeholder. Where the English says "{language} pocket guide" the Klingon says `{language} 'echletHom`, two bare nouns in a noun-noun compound, which needs no suffix at all. (2) **Capitalisation is phonemic**: `q` and `Q` are different consonants and `I` is a vowel while `i` is not a letter. So no template may uppercase or lowercase a placeholder, and none does. This is also why the respelling table for a Klingon reader cannot use the `caps` stress device -- see data/respell/rules/tlh__tlh-TA.json. WORD ORDER: Klingon is object-verb-subject and puts a time element first, so a template with a placeholder in the middle of a clause has to be written so the insert is a whole noun phrase in its own slot. `{target} → {source}` and `{language} Hol` are the two shapes used; nothing here asks a placeholder to sit inside a verb. WHAT IS NOT HERE: `format.reserve.ios` and `.android` are `'ayvon` and `'anDroy'`, which are transliterations of brand names rather than lexicon entries, and are the only two coinages in the catalogue. They are marked here rather than left to be discovered. Klingon has no attested word for a tax refund, so `quiz.interest.business.hint` carries the English `tax`. FINISHING, AND THREE STRINGS THIS FILE DOES NOT HAVE. The sheet-finishing control arrived after the rest of the catalogue and only seven of its ten strings could be written. `format.finish.fold`, `cut.hint.fold` and `studio.foldOrder` are absent because **there is no verb for `fold` in the published Klingon lexicon** -- TKD and KGT give `pe'` cut and `SIj` slit and nothing for creasing paper -- and the rule this file runs on is that no root here is an invention. The two hint strings would additionally need `panel` and `crease`, which are not there either. So those three fall back to English, which the overlay design does per string, and `npm run i18n` reports it: 319 of 322 rather than a coined verb on a button nobody can look up. `format.finish` itself is `nav Segh`, "kind of sheet" -- English names the operation and Klingon names the result, the same move `ngutlh Segh` makes for Typeface, and the second knowingly loose term here after `'uj`. `roman.okrand` and `roman.appendix-e` stay as printed: every one of the eleven `roman.*` keys already does, `Hepburn` and `McCune-Reischauer` included, so transcribing Okrand's name while leaving Hepburn's alone would make one menu disagree with itself. Whether pIqaD changes that was the question, and the answer is that the menu labels a column of *Latin* letters and this catalogue is romanised Klingon throughout -- the interface is the app's chrome, not the card. STUDIO, EXPORT AND PREVIEW PASS -- the forty-eight format.head*/export./picker./popup./quick./preview.lock/studio.moreActions keys, of which twenty are here and twenty-eight are not, and the twenty-eight fall into four groups with one reason each. THE TAB, and it takes eighteen of them. format.headFill (8), format.headReach (7) and format.headSpan (9 -- the whole family, which this file never had) all name one object: the coloured projection on the edge of a card that lets a fanned stack be read from the side, the tab on a file divider rather than a tab in a browser. **There is no Klingon word for a tab.** Nothing in the Klingonska dict.zdb the ornament note cites covers a projecting marker, and the two nouns the shapes need are missing beside it: no corner and no strip. {HeH} is an edge and {Dop} a side, and neither is the thing. Naming the positions instead would not save headSpan, because the bare direction words are already spent one control away -- format.head.left/.center/.right are poS, botlh, nIH -- and two controls under one set of labels is the fault the board note refuses at board.notANumber. So all eighteen fall back, and the two head keys that do not name a tab are written: format.headColour is qalmuS and format.headColour.default is motlh, this file's fourth spend of motlh after format.priority.core, format.theme.reference and format.padding.normal, and unavoidable, there being one word. THE OTHER TEN. format.headSlot.theme is out because there is no noun for a theme or a topic: the board note already records that {ghu'} "situation" stands in where English says board or topic, and a face's thematic group is not a situation. format.reserveHint is out because it names the lock screen's buttons, and THERE IS NO KLINGON WORD FOR BUTTON is already the ruling this file runs on -- {jIH} would give the screen and {ngaQ} "be locked" the lock, but the sentence cannot be finished. preview.lockDate is out because Klingon has no month names: data/lang/tlh/time.csv carries the six weekday names from the Saarbruecken qepHom'a' 2013 release and Monday is DaSjaj, but {jar} is glossed "month (Klingon)" and no Gregorian month can be named, so the mock would read DaSjaj 15 September. preview.lockTime is out because 9:41 is digits and a colon in Klingon too, so the English floor is already the right rendering and writing it again would only hide that. WHAT IS WRITTEN, and the four rewordings in it. export.asZip drops *download*, for which there is no verb, and says Hoch yIpol: wa' .zip "save everything: one .zip", the colon apposition cut.hint.shortEdge already uses; .zip stays Latin as every initialism in this file does. export.pages drops "one at a time" and "all together" for wa' yIpol, pagh Hoch yIpol "save one, or save all", which is what the two buttons under it do; {count} precedes an unsuffixed tenwal per TKD 5.2, as format.facesTitle already does. picker.budgetTitle drops the second clause -- "a row that repeats one already on counts for less" -- because Klingon's comparative is the {law'}/{puS} frame and cannot be hung on a relative clause without a starred suffix; what is left is wevmey 'ar pollu'. wa'DIch wevmey lI'qu'bogh lanlu', with the NOUN VERB-bogh order format.columnsShown already uses at warmey cha'lu'bogh. quick.nothingToExport is first person, vay' vIngeHlaHbe' "I cannot send anything", rather than an indefinite subject, because this file does not stack -lu' under -laH -- the same repair editor.damaged's vIlaDlaHbe' makes. popup.editText and popup.editing are built on {choH}, which is what editor.edit already says, and deliberately not on the {DI'} this file spends at tree.editRow, studio.discardEdits and studio.imported: {DI'} is not in dict.zdb in any part of speech, and -DI' is a type-9 verb suffix, so the three existing strings need checking against the post-2012 qepHom releases this note's source list names. ONE EXISTING STRING IS WRONG, recorded here rather than changed in this pass: format.cardWidth says 'echletHom vaS, and {vaS} is TKDa's noun for a hall or assembly hall. dict.zdb has no <wide> or <width> entry at all, so there is no Klingon word for width and that key should probably join the absent ones. THE TWO GALLERY KEYS. gallery.converse is ja'chuqmeH, the bare -meH label shape this file already spends on jatlhmeH, lengmeH, je'meH, ja'chuqmeH (board.docTitle) and lISmeH; the imperative was considered and rejected, because -chuq demands a plural subject (TKD 4.2.1) and a button addresses one reader, so peja'chuq would tell the reader and somebody else to confer. ja'chuqmeH mu'tlheghmey in gallery.tagline takes the noun-modifying purpose clause straight from TKD's own ja'chuqmeH rojHom. gallery.tagline is reworded and loses three modifiers -- *quick reference*, *curated* and the tree -- because there is no noun for a reference, none for curation, and {Sor} is a literal tree that this file will not stretch into a data structure; what is kept is both halves of the sentence, the printed card and the live board: 'echletHommey tIchenmoH, tIpol 'ej tIghItlh; pagh DaH ja'chuqmeH mu'tlheghmey tIHot. *print* is {ghItlh}, which HolQeD-02-4 p.18 glosses as the physical act of marking upon something, and which gallery.docTitle already spends the same way. MESSAGE-SCREEN PASS -- board.slow, board.switchTopic, board.switchLanguage and the nine display.* keys: ten of twelve written, two absent, every root checked against the Klingonska dict.zdb (2012-01-27 build, 2732 words). New roots, all dict.zdb: QIt (slowly, adverbial), -qa' (resume, do again, type 3), naDev (here), Doch (thing, noun [2]; [1] is the verb be rude), chu' (engage, activate a device, verb [2.1]; the same spelling is also be new), -Ha' (undo, rover), ghoj (learn), bIng (area below); bID (half) and Do (velocity) looked up and not spent. THE TWO ABSENT, both for the ruling this file already runs on -- THERE IS NO KLINGON WORD FOR BUTTON: display.speak is "Speak, and the half-speed button beside it" and display.turn is "the control that turns the sentence sideways", and each is a checkbox whose whole label is the name of a control. The editor keys dodged this by writing about the sentence instead of the control, but a checkbox that hides or shows a control cannot be renamed after the sentence it acts on, and the alternative -- ghogh for the speak toggle -- is already display.voice one row below, the two-controls-under-one-label fault board.notANumber refuses. Both fall back to English. For the next agent: the screen itself is not the problem; jIH [1] is dict.zdb's viewing screen and this pass spends it twice, each time with a suffix (jIHDaq, jIHvam) so the pronoun jIH [2] "me" cannot be read, as the interface-strings pass required. FOUR REWORDINGS. board.slow drops half speed for slowly, QIt yIjatlhqa': bID and Do are both dict.zdb but "at half velocity" would need a locative on an abstract noun that no canon sentence models, and QIt is TKD's own adverb; yIjatlh is board.speak. board.switchTopic and board.switchLanguage say "choose another situation / language", latlh ghu' yIwIv and latlh Hol yIwIv, because the control opens a list to choose from and choH would read as edit, which is what editor.edit already spends it on; ghu' is board.pickTopic's word. display.heading is a question, QIn jIHDaq nuq 'anglu' "on the message screen, what is shown" -- QIn (message) is the board note's KGT root, the locative goes first (TKD 6.1), and nuq takes the zero prefix under -lu' -- the same bare-question heading shape board.time's nuq rep already uses. display.lede drops hold out for show, and pronunciation for jatlhmeH mu'mey, the say-it-like column's own label: naDev Hoch: vay'vaD jIHvam Da'angbogh (everything here: this screen you show to someone, the colon apposition cut.hint.shortEdge uses) / Doch Dalo'be'bogh yIchu'Ha' (deactivate the thing you do not use; the relative clause carries Doch as its head noun because a headless -bogh clause is not grammatical) / pagh Hol DaghojtaHchugh jatlhmeH mu'mey yIchu' (or, if you are learning the language, activate the say-it words; -chugh clause first per TKD 6.2.2, pagh as the sentence conjunction). REUSE. display.roman and display.ipa mirror field.title.respell and field.title.ipa: jatlhmeH, ngutlhmeylIj and jatlhmeH, IPA ngutlhmey. ngutlh is not in the 2012 dict.zdb -- it is a later qep'a' word inside this note's stated source list -- and is kept only because it is already this file's settled word for a letter at field.roman, field.title.roman, field.title.ipa and format.romanisation; a reviewer who wants the file dict.zdb-only should change all five together. display.owner is mu'tlhegh bIngDaq mu'meylIj, your words below the sentence, with -lIj because mu' is not a language user (TKD 3.3.4). display.voice is ghogh, speech.*'s word. display.voiceAuto is wIv De'wI', the computer chooses, with the bare 3rd-3rd zero prefix: motlh (default) was considered and passed over because it is already spent four times and this option is a choice being made rather than a standard being kept. ONE THING A REVIEWER MAY DISPUTE: naDev Hoch for "everything here" -- TKD glosses Hoch as everything on its own and naDev as here, and the two are juxtaposed rather than compounded; if that reads as "all of here", Hoch alone before the colon loses nothing. SIGNAL-IN-MORSE PASS, thirteen keys, all thirteen written -- the first pass in this catalogue to add a string rather than only refuse or rework one. Two new attested nouns make it possible: {Degh} "medal, emblem, symbol, insignia" (TKDa 1992, dict.zdb id mVQ) and {'ul Sech} "flashlight" (TNK 2011-11-02 email, a noun-noun phrase, literally "electricity-torch"), neither spent anywhere else in this file. format.headSlot.logo is Phraselet Degh, N1 N2 = N1's N2 exactly as 'echletHom vaS (card width) already reads, so the brand name takes Degh as its head the same way a card takes a width. THE VERB THIS PASS ADDS: {wovmoH}, causative of {wov} "be light, be bright" (TKD, colour) with -moH (TKD 4.2.2), the same derivation dict.zdb already commits to in {wovmoHwI'} "light, for illumination" (BoP 1998) -- a light-MAKER presupposes a verb make-light, so wovmoH is not coined here, only used bare for the first time. yIwovmoH, "light it up", is gallery.signal and signal.start both, per the English note that the two may share a word. This narrows rather than reverses the _board_note's ruling on boards.emergency.sos: that entry needed a TRANSITIVE flash-SOS, object and all, and wov bare cannot take one; nothing here asks wovmoH to take an object, an imperative with the zero object prefix being a complete Klingon sentence on its own. Worth a second look by whoever next opens beacon.sos, but not changed here, being outside this pass's thirteen keys. signal.stop is yImev, mev (TKD) already spent at board.dismiss and beacon.dismiss. board.rate is jatlhmeH Do, "speed for speaking": Do "velocity" (TKD) was looked up and left unspent by the interface-strings pass's own note and is spent now. drill.reveal reworks "See answer" to yI'ang, "reveal it": jang is TKD's verb for answer/reply and has no attested noun reading (board.canAnswer already spends it only as a verb, lujanglaH), so the object is dropped rather than a noun coined for it, and 'ang "show, reveal" (TKD) is already this file's word for revealing content at display.lede. This is the first drill.* key in the catalogue; the rest of the practice-quiz screen (drill.check, drill.start, drill.kind and the other thirty-odd) has never been attempted here and stays English -- one word translated on an otherwise-English screen is not a regression, since the fallback is per-key. THE MORSE NOUN: {ngoq} "code" (TKD 1985) is real and unspent; "Morse" has no Klingon Wikipedia to attest a compound against, so Morse ngoq is composed the way every phrase in this file is composed -- attested headwords plus documented grammar -- rather than attested as a fixed term the way sv's Morsealfabetet or tr's Mors alfabesi are. Flagged here rather than hidden: a reviewer who wants the stricter, Wikipedia-attested bar the other twelve languages in this batch used would leave signal.heading, signal.docTitle, signal.unsayable and the section-titles row blank instead. signal.heading and signal.docTitle are the bare noun Morse ngoq and Morse ngoq — Phraselet, dropping "Signal in" the way every other *.title in this file is a bare topic noun rather than a verb phrase (He, poH, Soj); the em dash order matches board.docTitle, not gallery.docTitle, because en.json's own signal.docTitle puts the description first as board.docTitle's does. signal.message is QInlIj, "your message" (QIn, KGT, already this file's word at display.heading; -lIj rather than -wIj because a message is not a language-user, TKD 3.3.4). signal.received is ngoq DaSuqbogh, "the code you received" (Suq "acquire, get", TKD, already spent in the interface-strings pass; object relative clause, head noun first, as vISopbe'bogh Soj already reads). signal.unsayable is Morse ngoq Hutlhbogh ngutlhmey: {chars}, "the letters Morse code lacks: {chars}" -- Hutlh "lack, be without" (TKW/KGT, already spent) heads an object relative clause on ngutlhmey (this file's letter/glyph word), and {chars} sits after the colon per this file's own apposition device (cut.hint.shortEdge, export.asZip) rather than agreeing with anything. signal.lede rewords rather than translates line for line: yIghItlh nuq DajatlhnISbogh. Morse ngoq lulo'taH jIH 'ul Sech je, nuv laDlaHmeH. SOS: wa' Hot. -- "Write what you need to say. The screen and the flashlight use Morse code, so a person can read it. SOS: one touch." jIH 'ul Sech je is X Y je for "X and Y" (TKD), the shape colour.money's Huch Soj je already uses; lu- agrees with the two-noun subject; the -meH clause carries the readable-speed fact as a purpose ("so a person can read it") rather than as the noun Do, which would need a case device this file has no worked example for on an abstract noun -- the same reasoning board.slow's note gives for avoiding a locative on poH. Hot "touch" (TKD) is beacon.dismiss's word, reused for the tap. SECTION-TITLES ROW: morse-code,Morse ngoq is added on the same composed-not-attested basis as the two docTitle/heading keys above, and the same flag applies. INTERFACE-STRINGS PASS, THIRTY-FIVE KEYS. format.card.passportClosed/passportOpen are leng chaw' SoQ and leng chaw' poS: leng chaw' is TNK's own word for a passport (already at hotel-words.passport and border-customs.passport-control), SoQ "be closed" and poS "be open" are both TKD and both already attested in the corpus at common-signs.closed(-off) and common-signs.open-on; poS is also this file's word for "left" (format.head.left), a genuine TKD homograph and not a collision, since the two senses never share a control. format.theme.dark and theme.dark both spend Hurgh (TKD, "be dark", already at hike's trail-conditions.can-we-return-before-dark); theme.light is wov, this file's word for bright/light since the Morse pass's wovmoH. format.fold and its three options are absent for the same reason format.finish.fold already is: no verb for fold in the published lexicon. display.theme and theme.system are also absent: there is no word for "appearance" and no verified attested construction for "match the device" -- an honest gap rather than an invented one. BOARDS. boards.lodging.title is mebpa' (hotel-basics.are-any-rooms-available); .requests is vItlhob... (I request it...), tlhob "ask, request" TKD, already the root of section-titles' tlhobmeH mu'mey; .requestsTitle and boards.pharmacy.otcTitle share nuq DaneH "what do you want" (neH already wantLabel's verb), because the English is the same question twice. .problem is qay' pa'... , reusing room-problems.there-is-a-problem-with-the-room word for word; .problemTitle and boards.pharmacy.symptomsTitle share the bare qay' "problem", again one English question answered once. .laundry/.laundryTitle both spend section-titles' own Sut Say'moHmeH, the button taking the ellipsis the heading does not, as English does for the same pair. boards.sights.title, .entrance and .entranceTitle are absent: no word for sights, entrance or exit. .payment is jIDIl... (I pay.... DIl "pay" TKD, shop.csv's jIDIlpu'); .paymentTitle is chaw' DIlmeH "for paying the ticket". boards.pharmacy.title is section-titles' own Hergh ngevwI'. .symptoms, .dosage, .dosageTitle, .allergies and .allergiesTitle are absent: the pharmacy corpus has one row (jIwuQ, headache) and no word for a generic "feel", a dose, or an allergy. gallery.wantLabel gains 'ej, TKD's clause conjunction (already spent nine times in this file, e.g. quiz.interest.food's yISop 'ej yIje'), giving "...'ej jIjatlh vIneH", "...and I want to speak": speak_label is a full clause (jIjatlh) rather than a noun, so the pairing needs the conjunction English's own fix now supplies. INTERFACE-STRINGS ADDENDUM (personal.replace, personal.failed): both added, built only from roots and suffixes already used elsewhere in this file -- ghaj "to have" (TKD), choH "to change" with -DI' "when, as soon as" instead of the -pu' this file already puts on the same verb, Qaw' "to destroy" with the indefinite-subject -lu' this file already uses in personal.gone, chegh "to return" (TKD) with -pu', and the vI-...-'a' question pattern personal.confirm already ends on. format.theme.parchment is left out: no lexicon entry for parchment as a material or a colour name, and no root here is invented.

_ornament_note: Style labels use descriptive editorial paraphrases: mIllogh Segh (picture type), porDu' mIllogh (leaf picture), tlheghmey mIllogh (rope picture), Hov QuQ (star engine). These are not canonical names for the designs. yu'egh (wave), tlhegh (rope), Hov (star) and QuQ (engine) are TKD vocabulary; see https://klingonska.org/dict/. The low-ink hint says ordinary rules are used with little ink, and the chosen picture type returns when little ink is no longer used.
_board_note: Conversation-board and beacon strings. Every root is TKD or its addendum, as in the rest of this file: jang (answer, reply), SoQ (be closed), laj (accept), mI' (number), ghItlh (write), mev (stop, cease), Hot (touch, feel), poH (period of time), tup (minute), rep (hour), jaj (day), ghap (or, joining nouns) and 'ar (how many, how much -- TKD 6.4) are TKD; naQ (be full, be whole, be entire) and latlh (additional one, other one) are TKDA. beacon.help is ghoQaH, the canon form data/lang/tlh/emergency.csv already carries for emergency-medical.help (src=Star Trek VI): its object is plural, so it says "help us" rather than "help", and it stays romanised because that row carries no pIqaD either. TWO STRINGS ARE REWORDED rather than translated, because the English is not sayable. board.amount is poH 'ar, "how much time": 'ar follows the noun it counts, so a bare "how many" is not a Klingon phrase, and the corpus already composes it this way at time-scheduling.how-long-does-it-take. beacon.dismiss is mevmeH yIHot, "touch it so that it stops", which drops "anywhere" -- jIH is the viewing screen, but it is also the pronoun "me", so jIH yIHot would read as "touch me". WHAT IS NOT HERE: beacon.sos. SOS is a Morse sequence rather than an abbreviation of words, and every roman.* key in this file already leaves a standards initialism as printed, so the Latin letters fall back from English unchanged. SECOND PASS -- the clock and the bare number, all six added. board.atTime is rep, TKD's noun for an hour, which is how canon states a time of day (wa'vatlh rep is 01:00); the duration tile beside it keeps poH, TKD's noun for a period of time, so the two tiles carry the clock/duration contrast on Okrand's own pair of words and nothing is compounded. board.time is nuq rep "what hour?", the form data/lang/tlh/time.csv already carries at time-scheduling.what-time-is-it. board.number and board.otherNumber are the bare mI'. board.notATime is rep yIwIv "choose the hour": wIv (choose, select) is TKD, and the object-then-imperative shape is the one mI' naQ yIghItlh already uses. board.notANumber repeats board.notAnAmount word for word, because the two English strings are the same string. RESIDUAL RISK, recorded rather than hidden: hours of duration are also counted in rep (cha' rep, two hours), so rep... is unambiguous only because latlh poH... stands beside it. THIRD PASS -- the board's own chrome and the eight topic names, fifty-two of the fifty-four. Roots new to this note, every one from the published lexicon: chegh (return, TKD), ghu' (situation, TKD), Hoch (all, TKD), QIn (message, KGT), tetlh (roll, scroll, list, KGT), ghum (sound an alarm, TKD), buS (concentrate on, focus on, TKD), chIl (lose, TKDA), Seng (trouble, noun, TKD), rop (disease, noun, TKD), 'oy' (ache, pain, noun, TKD), qaS (occur, happen, TKD), ghaj (have, TKD), ngaS (contain, TKD), Sop (eat, TKD), je' (buy, TKD), leng (travel, TKD), ghom (meet, TKD), ghorgh (when?, TKD), nuv (person, TKD), Soj (food, TKDA), He (course, route, TKD), poH (period of time, TKD), chach (emergency, TKD), tlhe' (turn, TKD), ruch (proceed, TKDA), leS (rest, relax, TKD), maj (good, exclamation, TKD 5.5), pagh (or, between sentences, TKD 5.3, and the numeral zero, TKD), volchaH (shoulder, TKD), mong (neck, TKD), porgh (body, TKD), 'ay' (section, part, TKD), and lupwI' (bus, CK and KGT), ra'wI' (commander, TKD) and yaH (duty station, TKD) in the compounds data/lang/tlh/travel.csv already uses for a taxi and a platform. THE EIGHT TOPIC NAMES say what this catalogue and data/registry/section-titles/tlh.csv already say rather than coining beside them: chach is colour.alert and the emergency-medical section title; He, poH and Soj are the directions, time-scheduling and food-ordering section titles; nuvpu' yIghom is quiz.interest.social word for word and lengmeH is colour.move word for word; je'meH takes the -meH label shape from the shopping section title je'meH mu'mey, the same shape jatlhmeH and lengmeH already use. Soj names the food and not the act of dining out, and lengmeH the purpose and not the getting-around, because Klingon has no noun for either -- recorded here rather than compounded into existence. FIVE STRINGS ARE REWORDED. board.someMissing drops "on this board": {count} mu'tlhegh mughlu'pu'be', and mughlu'pu'be' is gallery.notTranslated unchanged; a number precedes an unsuffixed noun (TKD 5.2), so the placeholder cannot force a plural. board.noBoards is pagh ghu' tu'lu', "there are no situations" -- pagh is TKD's zero, tu'lu' the existential food-ordering.is-a-table-available already uses, and ghu' is what board.pickTopic and board.allTopics call a board, because there is no noun for a panel of buttons. board.turn drops "sideways": mu'mey yItlhe'moH, "make the words turn"; jIr (rotate) is KGT but the control is a toggle and not a direction, so tlhe' with the causative -moH (TKD 4.2.2) is used. boards.emergency.attention is yIghum, "sound the alarm", there being no verb for attracting attention. boards.emergency.lostTitle is Seng, "trouble", above the narrower tile vIchIlpu' "I have lost it": the English pairs a narrow button with a broad heading, and this keeps that relation without a noun for theft. board.wrongPair is object-verb-subject with both placeholders in bare noun-phrase slots and no suffix on either, as the rule at the top of this note requires: {language} Hol mu'tlheghmey ghajbe' {board}. board.docTitle is ja'chuqmeH (ja'chuq, discuss, confer, TKD) because there is no noun for a conversation, and it takes the same -meH label shape. board.menu is tetlh, a list: HIDjolev is TKD's own gloss for "menu" but it is a bill of fare, and the control opens a list of settings. THE ONE SPLIT THAT DOES NOT SURVIVE is boards.spa.focusOn over boards.body.*. Klingon puts the object before the verb, so a heading above its own objects has them in the wrong order; the heading is instead the complete clause porgh 'ay' yIbuS, "focus on a body part", and the four buttons are possessed nouns under it -- volchaHDu'wIj, DubwIj, mongwIj, qamDu'wIj, with -Du' for body parts and -wIj for a possessor of a thing (TKD 3.3.2, 3.3.4). WHAT IS NOT HERE. boards.spa.title: there is no word for massage anywhere in the published lexicon, and data/lang/tlh carries no massage-spa rows at all, so the board's name falls back to English whole. boards.emergency.sos: the English is "Flash SOS" and there is no verb for flashing -- boch is to shine and wov is to be bright, and neither takes the Latin letters as an object -- so it falls back for the same reason beacon.sos does. INTERFACE-STRINGS PASS -- the forty-seven editor./speaker./speech./personal./settings. keys, of which forty-seven are here and none are absent, which is the opposite of the finishing pass above and worth saying why. New roots, all dict.zdb (https://klingonska.org/dict/, the source the ornament note already names) unless marked: per (label, n. and v., TKD), Hutlh (lack, be without, TKW/KGT), jan (device, TKD), De'wI' (computer, TKD), ghogh (voice, TKD), HablI' (data transceiving device, TKD), mugh (translate, TKD), Sam (locate, seek and find, TKDa), laD (read, TKD), 'ang (show, reveal, TKD), jatlh (say, speak, TKD), nID (attempt, try, TKD), poQ (demand, require, TKD), mev (stop, cease, TKD), teb (fill, TKD), chu' (engage, activate a device, TKD), teq (remove, take off, TKD), Qaw' (destroy, TKD), vIH (move, be in motion, TKDa), Dung/bIng (area above/below, TKD), chel (add, TKD), tam (exchange, substitute, replace, TKD), tI' (fix, repair, TKD), lIS (adjust, TKD), motlh (be usual, be standard, TKD), loy (guess, TKD), wuv (depend on, rely on, TKD), Del (describe, TKD), wot (verb, TKD), loD (man, TKD), be' (woman, TKD), ratlh (remain, TKD), qeng (carry, convey, TKD), Suq (acquire, get, TKD), mej (leave, depart, TKDa), qaS (occur, happen, TKD), qeq (practice, train, TKD), Qu' (task, TKD), pItlh (done, all finished, TKD 5.5), chay' (how?, TKD), not (never, TKD), nuv (person, TKD), jIH (viewing screen, TKD), vay' (anything, anyone, TKD), Hoch (all, every, TKD), neH (only, merely, TKD), latlh (other one, TKDa), pagh (nothing, and the sentence conjunction or, TKD 5.3). FIVE TERMS FIXED HERE. jIH is the screen -- one panel of the reader's own buttons, not the device -- and the pronoun collision the board note records (jIH is also "me") cannot arise, because every use here carries a type-4 demonstrative or a case suffix: jIHvam, jIHvamvo', jIHvamDaq, jIHmeyDaq, and a pronoun takes neither. jan is the device the data lives on and De'wI' the computer that does or does not do a thing (translate, speak aloud) -- Klingon has no word for an app or a browser, so the two failure messages that name one in English name the computer instead. mu'tlhegh is the reader's own button, because THERE IS NO KLINGON WORD FOR BUTTON: nothing in the lexicon covers a pressable control, and the whole editor family is therefore written about the sentence rather than the control that shows it, which is also what the phrase actually is. lISmeH is Settings, taking the bare -meH label shape the file already spends on jatlhmeH, lengmeH, je'meH and ja'chuqmeH; wIvmey stays Options at quick.optionsLabel, and personal.heading says wIvmeywIj for "your settings" because Klingon has one word where English has two and the two controls are on different pages. THE THREE LOAD-BEARING STRINGS ARE CONCRETE, not softened. editor.noTranslation ends vay'Daq ngeHlu'be', "it is not sent anywhere" -- ngeHlu'be' rather than the noun pagh, because pagh is also the conjunction "or" and would be read as one at the head of its clause. personal.lede opens janvamDaq neH ratlh Hoch, "everything remains only on this device". personal.confirm is a question with Qaw' "destroy" in it, names all three things being destroyed, and keeps the clause that only the saved data comes back. editor.damaged keeps both halves: pagh tamlu'pu' "nothing has been replaced", then tI'lu'pa' latlh mu'tlheghmey tIchelQo' "do not add more before it is repaired". SIX STRINGS ARE REWORDED. editor.owner and editor.listener are the bare HollIj and latlh Hol, "your language" and "the other language": Klingon has no way to head a field with "what it means" that is shorter than the field. editor.noTranslation drops "paste or" and "yourself" and says yIghItlh, "write it". editor.label is the bare per, because ngaj is short in duration and run is short in stature and neither is short in extent -- there is no Klingon word for a short piece of text. speech.remote-only drops "the only". speech.unmapped drops "anywhere", so it is Holvetlh ghogh tu'lu'be' "that language's voice is not found" against speech.no-voice's Holvetlh ghogh Hutlh janvam "this device lacks that language's voice" -- the two stay distinguishable, which is the whole point of having both. personal.loaded reads the English "Nothing was changed until now" as the claim that the import is all-or-nothing and says qaSpa' pagh choHlu'pu', "before it happened nothing was changed". ONE COLLAPSE THE LANGUAGE FORCES: speaker.speaker_gender.why says wot alone where the English says "a verb or an adjective", because Klingon adjectives are verbs and DIp is a noun -- there is no word for adjective and coining one to translate a sentence about other languages would be the invention this file does not make. Its two examples are the corpus's own rows, DaqwIj vISovbe' (building-help.i-am-lost) and qatlho' (social-basics.thank-you). GRAMMAR, checked rather than assumed: no placeholder carries a suffix; {count} and {phrases} precede unsuffixed nouns (TKD 5.2) as the note above requires; -lu' is never stacked under -laH, because KGT p.181 has the dedicated -la' for that and this file does not spend a starred suffix -- editor.damaged is therefore first person, vIlaDlaHbe'. TWO TYPOS FIXED IN PASSING: gallery.loading and studio.loadingTree read Sammu'taH, and there is no -mu' verb suffix in Klingon; every other indefinite-subject form in this file is spelt -lu' (mughlu'pu'be', pollu'taH, chenmoHlu'taH, cha'lu'taH, lanlu'taH), so both are now Samlu'taH. Left alone but recorded: gallery.saveFailed's pollu'laHbe' stacks two type-5 suffixes, which KGT p.181's -la' exists to avoid; it is widely written this way and changing it is a separate judgement. SECTION TITLES, in data/registry/section-titles/tlh.csv: five of the seven that were missing are now there. dietary-needs is vISopbe'bogh Soj, "the food I do not eat", a relative clause because the section is a list of refusals rather than a topic. quick-directions is He mu'mey, "route words", the X mu'mey glossary shape the file already uses at poH mu'mey, qach mu'mey and Daq mu'mey, beside the plain He that names the directions section. accessibility is vIHlaHmeH, "so that one can move", which covers both halves of Access + mobility in one -meH clause. color-size-returns is nobHa'meH mu'mey, "words for giving back" (nobHa', TKW p.189/KGT, tagged economics), and it drops colour and size: qalmuS is available but THERE IS NO KLINGON NOUN FOR SIZE -- juv is to measure and 'ab is to have a length of, both verbs -- so a three-item list cannot be built, and a heading naming only colour and size would misname the return-and-exchange half of the section. board-answers is mujangmeH mu'mey, "words for him or her to answer me", which is the traveller's point of view and is kept apart from quick-responses' jangmeH mu'mey, the traveller's own. STILL ABSENT, and falling back to English on the printed sheet: massage-spa, for the reason boards.spa.title is absent -- no word for massage anywhere in the lexicon -- and keeping it absent is what makes the sheet and the board agree; and tax-refund, because there is no word for tax, which quiz.interest.business.hint already records.SECTION-TITLE PASS, and it opens with a correction to the paragraph above. **The five titles that paragraph reports as "now there" were never written to data/registry/section-titles/tlh.csv.** The note landed and the CSV edit did not; the file still held fifty-four rows against en.csv's sixty-one, and the seven it was missing were the same seven. They are there now, five of them, and the two that stay out stay out for a reason the row counts make stronger than the lexical one. dietary-needs is vISopbe'bogh Soj, quick-directions He mu'mey, color-size-returns nobHa'meH mu'mey and board-answers mujangmeH mu'mey, all four as that paragraph reasoned them. accessibility is **naw'**, not the vIHlaHmeH it proposed: vIH is motion and the section is not only about motion -- two of its nine rows are jIQoylaHchu'be' and jIleghlaHchu'be', hearing and sight, which a purpose clause about moving does not head -- while {naw'} is TKD's own noun for <access> and translates the head of the English "Access + mobility" exactly. It is an E-K-side headword, which is worth recording because that side of TKD is thinner evidence than the K-E side; the verb {naw'} "access" is there beside it, and a bare noun is this file's commonest title shape (Hol, De', pong, ghob, poH, Huch, Soj, He, veH, muD, chach) so it reads as one. THE TWO THAT STAY ABSENT, and the reason is now doubled. massage-spa and tax-refund have **no Klingon rows at all** -- data/lang/tlh carries nothing under either concept -- so a title there would head an empty panel, which is worse than an English heading over the same nothing. The lexical reasons still hold and are the ones that matter if rows ever arrive: there is no word for massage anywhere in the published lexicon, which is also why boards.spa.title is absent, and the sheet and the board therefore agree. For tax-refund the earlier claim needs narrowing: {rup} "fine, tax" is in TKD, so it is not true that Klingon has no word for tax -- what it has is a *verb*, with no noun for a tax and nothing at all for a refund, so quiz.interest.business.hint keeps its English tax for the same reason and the two records now agree. ONE THING A REVIEWER MAY DISPUTE. color-size-returns' heading says nobHa' where the section's own row color-size-returns.can-i-return-it says vItatlhlaH'a'. {tatlh} would have matched the row, but its source is the 1999-07-19 Okrand email, which the corpus admits (lex=KLI 1999.07.19) and this catalogue's stated source list -- TKD, its addendum, KGT, Talk Now!, qep'a' and qepHom'a' -- does not; {nobHa'} is TKW p.189/KGT and is inside it. Two synonyms for one act, one in the heading and one in the row, is the price of staying in range. CHECKED MECHANICALLY, as the earlier passes were: every token in the five new titles strips to a headword in the Klingonska dict.zdb the ornament note cites -- vI-Sop-be'-bogh, Soj, nobHa'-meH, mu'-mey, He, naw', mu-jang-meH -- and every codepoint the derived pIqaD column holds is in all four latin-*.ttf faces, so nothing new prints as a gap.
